However, the story clarifies that he spent the entire weekend at home resting and reading books, which indicates there was no actual family gathering. This suggests he fabricated the excuse to avoid the fishing activity without directly refusing his friend, which aligns with common social behavior to maintain politeness while declining an invitation. 

Option A is unlikely because there is no mention of planning a bigger party, and he stayed home alone. Option C is unsupported, as the story does not reference any professional award or attempts to hide success. Option D is also unsupported, as there is no indication he promised his wife to reduce workload or that the excuse was intended to demonstrate such a change. The most logical explanation is that he made up the family gathering excuse to avoid fishing without being rude.

STORY: Mr. Zhang is a busy lawyer, often works overtime until late at night. His old friend Mr. Li invites him to a weekend fishing activity. Mr. Zhang does not like fishing, so he tells Mr. Li that his wife arranges an important family gathering, he must attend. On the weekend, Mr. Zhang spends the whole day at home resting and reading books.
QUESTION: Why does Mr. Zhang say this?
OPTION-A: Mr. Zhang says this because he wants to give Mr. Li a surprise, in fact, he plans to arrange a bigger party privately.
OPTION-B: Mr. Zhang says this because he does not want to participate in the fishing activity, but does not want to directly refuse his friend, so he makes up the excuse of a family gathering.
OPTION-C: Mr. Zhang just finds out that he is going to receive an important professional award, he says these to hide his success, so as not to appear too proud.
OPTION-D: Mr. Zhang previously promises his wife to reduce the workload, he makes up the excuse of the gathering to show that he is trying to change.
